---

This release upgrades most of the Python dependencies to their latest versoins,
including upgrading Pydantic AI to version 2.
It also adopts ruff 0.16's expanded default lint ruleset (and the codebase to pass it),
and improves compatibility with newer Stripe API versions.

- **Upgraded most Python packages to their latest versions.**
  - The most notable update is upgrading Pydantic AI to version 2, which included minor changes to
    the AI and chat code for its new APIs.
- **Upgraded ruff to 0.16 and adopted its expanded default ruleset.**
  Projects now use ruff's default rules, enabling many additional rules.
  - Common categories of addressed errors include:
    - Translated error messages that contain variables now use `%` placeholders instead of f-strings,
      so the messages can be properly translated before the variables are substituted.
    - The AI weather demo tool now makes its geocoding request with an async HTTP client
      instead of a blocking `requests` call.
    - A few places now log to a named module logger instead of the root logger,
      and a couple of generic `Exception`s were replaced with more specific error classes.
    - The mutable-class-default rule (`RUF012`) is explicitly disabled,
      since it conflicts with common Django idioms.
- **Improved compatibility with newer Stripe API versions:**
  - Added a `subscription_cancels_at_period_end` helper that handles both the legacy `cancel_at_period_end`
    boolean and the newer `cancel_at` field, and updated the subscription views, webhooks,
    and wrappers to use it.
  - The subscription wrapper's `current_period_end` now falls back to the data on the subscription item
    when it isn't set on the subscription itself, as is the case in newer API versions.
  - Updated the ecommerce checkout helper to read the checkout session ID from `session.id`
    instead of the removed `session.stripe_id`.
  - Added tests covering the new behavior.
- Fixed the `upgrade-python-deps` skill to remove uv's cooldown marker from `uv.lock`.
  The previous version could cause later syncs to silently re-resolving packages to their newest versions.
